text:
Jess (acme-corp): Hey team, our dedicated endpoints are not scaling fast enough. Getting 429s and tail latency spikes since ~09:30 PDT :grimacing:
Sam (support): Sorry to hear that — can you confirm this is on your prod-dedicated cluster and whether min_replicas is >0?
Jess (acme-corp): Yes, prod-dedicated us-west2. Config: min_replicas=1, max_replicas=8. No billing notices on our side. We see a sustained 20rps and the pool stays at 1 for minutes.
Tess (customer-success): I can reproduce a similar pattern against a test account with same config. 429s appear when load ramps quickly.
Sam (support): Sharing logs and example curl to repro. @maya / @arthur can you triage?
Sam (support): ```bash
# repro load (simple)
for i in {1..60}; do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"input":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/dedicated/prod-xxxx/generate &
done
wait
```
Jess (acme-corp): Attaching request/response snippet from our client: 
```
POST /v1/dedicated/prod-xxxx/generate
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-Request-Id: r-12345
Body: {"error":"capacity_limited: no healthy replicas"}
```
Maya (eng-oncall): Looking at control-plane and autoscaler traces now. @lina any known probe suppression heuristics that could delay spinup?
Lina (eng-runtime): We do have a probe suppression window for back-to-back probe failures to avoid thrashing with registry pulls. But it should un-suppress after ~30s. Do you have autoscaler logs?
Sam (support): From control-plane: 
```
[autoscaler] 2026-03-15T16:30:12Z probe_timeout podprobe id=pod-abc status=timeout
[autoscaler] 2026-03-15T16:30:12Z suppressing_probes for pool=prod-xxxx holdoff_ms=45000 reason=image_pull_backoff
[attach] 2026-03-15T16:30:35Z attempt_attach failed quota=attach-rate limited=true
[autoscaler] 2026-03-15T16:31:02Z scale_decision min_replicas=1 desired=6 reason=latency_spike
```
Maya (eng-oncall): Hm probe suppression due to image pull/backoff + attach-rate limit. That holdoff_ms=45000 is larger than expected. Could be compounded by quota throttling on the cluster side.
Arthur (eng-platform): We rolled out a throttling patch last week that gates registry pulls per-tenant to avoid noisy neighbor storms. It's possible the gating interacts poorly with autoscaler's aggressive desired replicas.
Tess (customer-success): Customer reports no registry pull errors on their side. This looks internal.
Lina (eng-runtime): Two possible attack vectors: 1) attach-rate quota is too low for bursty ramps; 2) probe suppression holdoff gets extended if attach attempts keep failing, leading to multi-minute unresponsive warm-up.
Sam (support): Repro steps for eng: ramp 20->200 concurrent short requests, observe attach attempts and probe suppression.
Arthur (eng-platform): I can spin a staging run. Can someone drop the exact environment id?
Sam (support): env id: prod-xxxx (shared with customer). For staging use prod-stg-yyy.
Maya (eng-oncall): Quick mitigation we can do now: temporarily bump customer attach-rate quota and reduce probe suppression holdoff for that pool. Will that be safe? @arthur?
Arthur (eng-platform): For a one-off, yes. We'll coordinate with infra to raise the gating token bucket for prod-xxxx to allow faster attach.
Lina (eng-runtime): Also recommend increasing min_replicas to 2 for this tenant as an immediate SLO workaround while we root cause.
Tess (customer-success): I will propose that to the customer as a short-term change. They prefer not to increase costs but understand outage risk.
Sam (support): Next steps: @arthur to run staging repro and confirm attach-rate gating reproduction, @lina to instrument autoscaler to log extended suppression reasons, @maya to sign off on temporary quota bump, @tess to coordinate with customer on min_replicas change.
Arthur (eng-platform): I'll post results in this thread within the hour. :eyes:
deploy-bot: Deployment event: platform/registry-throttle-v2 rolled back for canary 3 after anomaly detection at 16:12 UTC.
Maya (eng-oncall): That rollback could explain why some pools still run the throttle-v2 behavior. Check canary rollout state.
Sam (support): Thanks everyone. Jess, we'll update here after the staging run and proposed config changes.
Jess (acme-corp): Appreciate the quick response. Fingers crossed. :crossed_fingers:
